{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the bottom line of the fish, stroke 2. It is the long belly outline that gives the picture its shape, and I started it at the nose join and traced it along the belly. I laid it in several batches, about 25 dominoes in the main pushes. Before the push, the standing dominoes were connected to the start: about 116 of 119 by my trace of the table. A fish needs both the top and the bottom outline to be recognizable, and I built the bottom one.

Execution: I picked one piece of work and stayed on it. I laid the belly steadily, then used close inspections to find where the chain looked weak. I stood dominoes back up where they had gone down and re-laid them from the stroke. I checked the belly joins in the final minutes so the run would fall cleanly from the start.

Collaboration: I said early that I had the bottom line and told the table when I was handing the tail end to Priya. I stepped back from that stretch so our hands didn't collide, and I stayed clear before the push so nothing got bumped. I also asked Tom to cover the joins so the work was split cleanly.

Leadership: I kept my stretch clearly claimed and communicated when it was done. I handed it off at the right moment and moved to quality checking rather than crowding the tail. I backed the fish plan as soon as it was proposed, which helped the table commit quickly with limited time.

My honest view is that the belly line was a central part of the picture, and I carried it from the nose until I passed the tail end on.", "my_share_percent": 25}
